intro: Two ceremonies on the wedding day. Here is what happens in each, and what to expect.

ceremonies.name: Anand Karaj
about: Anand Karaj is the Sikh marriage ceremony. It takes place in the presence of the Guru Granth Sahib, the Sikh scripture, which is treated as the living Guru and presides over the marriage.

There are no vows spoken between the couple and no exchange of rings. The marriage is carried entirely in four hymns — the Laavan — which are read aloud and then sung as the couple walks around the Guru Granth Sahib.

etiquette.title: Covering your head
etiquette.note: Cover your head. Scarves are available at the entrance.

etiquette.title: Tobacco and alcohol
etiquette.note: Please carry no tobacco or alcohol.

etiquette.title: Seating
etiquette.note: Seating is on the floor. Try not to point your feet toward the Guru Granth Sahib.

etiquette.title: During the hymns
etiquette.note: Please stay seated while the hymns are being sung.

sequence.name: Ardas
sequence.note: The opening prayer. The congregation stands.

sequence.name: Hukamnama
sequence.note: A passage is read at random from the Guru Granth Sahib — the Guru's word for the day.

sequence.name: Palla
sequence.note: The bride's father places one end of the groom's scarf into her hand. From here they are joined.

sequence.name: The four Laavan
sequence.note: Each hymn is read, then sung. During the singing the couple walks slowly, clockwise, around the Guru Granth Sahib.

sequence.name: Anand Sahib
sequence.note: A hymn of bliss, and the closing Ardas.

sequence.name: Karah Prasad
sequence.note: A sweet offering shared with everyone present. Please receive it with both hands.

meaning.title: The four Laavan
meaning.lead: Composed by Guru Ram Das. Each round is a stage of union.

items.name: First
items.note: A commitment to a righteous life together, and to the duties that come with it.

items.name: Second
items.note: The meeting with the true Guru. The self begins to dissolve.

items.name: Third
items.note: Detachment from what does not matter. Love for the divine grows.

items.name: Fourth
items.note: Harmony. The union is complete — of two people, and of the soul with the divine.

meaning.closing: When the fourth Laav ends, they are married.

ceremonies.name: Vivaah
about: The Hindu ceremony takes place beneath a mandap, around a sacred fire. Agni, the fire, is the witness — every vow is made in its presence, and it is what makes the marriage binding.
A priest guides the couple through a sequence of rites in Sanskrit. The heart of it is the phere, when the couple circles the fire together, and the saptapadi, the seven steps.

etiquette.title: Coming and going
etiquette.note: The ceremony runs long. Please come and go quietly as you need to.

etiquette.title: Shoes
etiquette.note: Remove your shoes before entering the mandap area.

etiquette.title: Seating
etiquette.note: Seating is close to the floor.

etiquette.title: The aisle
etiquette.note: Please keep the aisle clear for the families.

sequence.name: Milni
sequence.note: The two families meet formally for the first time and greet one another.

sequence.name: Varmala
sequence.note: The couple exchange garlands. The first thing they do as a couple, in front of everyone.

sequence.name: Kanyadaan
sequence.note: The bride's parents give her hand to the groom — the most emotional moment of the day for her family.

sequence.name: Havan
sequence.note: The sacred fire is lit. From here, Agni is the witness.

sequence.name: Mangal Phere
sequence.note: The couple circles the fire together, the groom leading, then the bride.

sequence.name: Saptapadi
sequence.note: Seven steps, seven promises — for food, strength, prosperity, happiness, family, the seasons, and lifelong friendship.

sequence.name: Sindoor & Mangalsutra
sequence.note: The groom marks her hair with sindoor and ties the mangalsutra. The marriage is complete.

meaning.title: The seven steps
meaning.lead: Saptapadi. One promise with each step.

items.name: Two
items.note: To grow strong together, in body and mind.

items.name: Three
items.note: To prosper, and to share what they have.

items.name: Four
items.note: To bring happiness and harmony to each other's families.

items.name: Five
items.note: To raise a family with care.

items.name: Six
items.note: To stay together through every season.

items.name: Seven
items.note: To remain friends, above all else.

meaning.closing: With the seventh step, they are married.
